Four additional analyses confirm the mechanism underlying SICA's failure. Extraction error taxonomy (Appendix~\ref{app:extraction}): 91.8\% of constraints are technically discriminative, but their discriminative direction mirrors the majority answer; 42.9\% of constraints are redundant across traces (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), quantifying how co-sourcing from the same model produces near-duplicate formalizations. Removing the 8.2\% non-discriminative constraints yields zero improvement. Constraint ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}): on Mistral-7B ($n = 804$, FOLIO + ProofWriter pooled), MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 94.4\% of predictions, with disagreements split nearly evenly (18 vs.\ 17); the solver's weighted satisfiability computation adds no value over simple constraint counting because constraint weights carry information redundant with vote counts (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). Per-domain, MAX-SAT provides a marginal edge in the intermediate-SC region (59.3\% vs.\ count-only 56.9\%) but actively hurts in the Type~C regime (36.5\% vs.\ 37.2\%), mirroring the regime-dependent pattern of SICA itself. Hyperparameter sensitivity (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}): $K = 12$ is the only setting with $\Delta > 2$\,pp among five $K$ values, and only $T = 0.7$ among four temperatures yields a positive effect; both peaks coincide with relatively low SC baselines rather than reflecting hyperparameter effects per se. Entropy decomposition (Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}): all SICA effects concentrate in high-entropy problems ($\Delta$ up to $+12.8$\,pp in the intermediate-SC region), but the direction depends on the accuracy regime---high entropy signals correctable uncertainty only when the model has partial knowledge.

1	\section{Discussion}
2	\label{sec:discussion}
3	
4	The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.
5	
6	Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.
7	
8	\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}) constitutes the primary finding of this paper. SC ($\kappa = 0.44$), Diverse-Prompt ($\kappa = 0.40$), and ICG ($\kappa = 0.47$) cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, forming a same-model ceiling: neither prompt variation nor independent constraint generation breaks the correlation. Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. This independence-accuracy trade-off is a fundamental Pareto frontier: methods that increase trace independence necessarily degrade accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. Crucially, this trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results---DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}---each bypass same-model self-extraction, trading simplicity for architectures that introduce genuinely independent signal.
9	
10	\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.
11	
12	\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects in this study are negative. Among nine SICA conditions, none reaches $p < 0.05$ (best $p = 0.092$); the four-seed replication yields $p = 0.092$, $0.070$, $1.0$, and $1.0$. In contrast, SICA degrades significantly on ProofWriter ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp, $p = 0.014$; $\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). McNemar's paired test on method-level interventions sharpens this asymmetry: three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance (Debate $p < 0.001$ on both datasets; Contrastive $p < 0.01$ on FOLIO), all negative, with discordant pairs heavily skewed toward correct$\to$wrong flips. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This pattern---zero significant positives, multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.
13	
14	\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} The method-level interventions that test the trade-off most directly use Mistral-7B. The trade-off itself is fundamental---it follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs---but its severity may vary with scale. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

1	\section{Analysis}
2	\label{sec:analysis}
3	
4	The regime-dependent pattern in \S\ref{sec:main-results} establishes \emph{where} SICA succeeds and fails. This section investigates \emph{why}: trace correlation quantifies the SC plateau (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}), supporting diagnostics confirm the mechanism (Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}), and remediation analysis reveals a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
5	
6	\subsection{Condorcet Effective-K}
7	\label{sec:effective-k}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:independence} reports Fleiss' $\kappa$ and Effective-K (Eq.~\ref{eq:effk}) across 15 conditions at $K = 12$. Among instruction-tuned models, $\kappa$ ranges from 0.21 to 0.82, yielding $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20\text{--}3.62$. Qwen3-14B in thinking mode reaches $\kappa = 0.91$ ($K_{\text{eff}} = 1.09$). Two conditions are jointly necessary for positive $\Delta$: sufficient $K_{\text{eff}}$ (Qwen conditions with $K_{\text{eff}} \leq 1.30$ never improve) and sufficient SC accuracy (Mistral on ProofWriter with the highest $K_{\text{eff}} = 3.62$ but SC $= 39\%$ produces significant degradation). 41	
42	Four additional analyses confirm the mechanism underlying SICA's failure. Removing the 8.2\% non-discriminative constraints yields zero improvement. Constraint ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}): on Mistral-7B ($n = 804$, FOLIO + ProofWriter pooled), MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 94.4\% of predictions, with disagreements split nearly evenly (18 vs.\ 17); the solver's weighted satisfiability computation adds no value over simple constraint counting because constraint weights carry information redundant with vote counts (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). Per-domain, MAX-SAT provides a marginal edge in the intermediate-SC region (59.3\% vs.\ count-only 56.9\%) but actively hurts in the Type~C regime (36.5\% vs.\ 37.2\%), mirroring the regime-dependent pattern of SICA itself. \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}) constitutes the primary finding. SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG form a same-model ceiling at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate breaks through only at catastrophic accuracy cost (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). This trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm} each bypass same-model self-extraction.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects are negative: zero of nine SICA conditions reaches $p < 0.05$, while ProofWriter degradation ($p = 0.014$; $p = 0.011$) and three of six method-level conditions (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}) reach significance, all negative. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This asymmetry---zero significant positives against multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} Method-level interventions use Mistral-7B; whether larger models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question, though the trade-off itself follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs. The Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) explains this plateau: same-model traces are correlated voters, so additional samples carry diminishing independent information. Symbolic constraints in first-order logic (FOL) appear to offer a way forward, but when extracted by the same model, they inherit the traces' correlation structure. We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}. We study it through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts FOL constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT. Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances and four-seed replication, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting. A directional positive trend (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp; $p < 0.10$ in 2 of 4 seeds, none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears only in one model on one dataset at 50--55\% SC baseline. Oracle controls with gold FOL confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound, yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of the oracle ceiling. The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off revealed by Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods: Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling the effective sample size, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. Methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches. The $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling, and $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic. The bottleneck is structural at the 7B--14B scale tested; whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome it remains open.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}) constitutes the primary finding. SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG form a same-model ceiling at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate breaks through only at catastrophic accuracy cost (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). This trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm} each bypass same-model self-extraction.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects are negative: zero of nine SICA conditions reaches $p < 0.05$, while ProofWriter degradation ($p = 0.014$; $p = 0.011$) and three of six method-level conditions (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}) reach significance, all negative. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This asymmetry---zero significant positives against multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} Method-level interventions use Mistral-7B; whether larger models shift the Pareto frontier is an open question, though the trade-off itself follows from the correlation structure of same-model outputs. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

toolUseResult.originalFile: Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces is the dominant test-time aggregation strategy for LLMs, but accuracy gains saturate as sample count grows. The Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) explains this plateau: same-model traces are correlated voters, so additional samples carry diminishing independent information. Symbolic constraints in first-order logic (FOL) appear to offer a way forward, but when extracted by the same model, they inherit the traces' correlation structure. We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}. We study it through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts FOL constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT. Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances and four-seed replication, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting. A directional positive trend (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp; $p < 0.10$ in 2 of 4 seeds, none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears only in one model on one dataset at 50--55\% SC baseline. Oracle controls with gold FOL confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound, yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of the oracle ceiling. The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off revealed by Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods: Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling the effective sample size, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. Methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches. The $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling, and $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic. The bottleneck is structural at the 7B--14B scale tested; whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome it remains open.
